"Always! Allah Al-Qabidh withholds with wisdom!"

## What Can We Learn?

✅ Allah withholds with wisdom - Not to harm us, but to protect us

✅ Trust Allah's withholding - It's for our benefit

✅ Sometimes "no" is better than "yes" - Allah knows what we don't know

✅ Be patient when Allah withholds - There's wisdom in it

## Activity: Think About It!

🌟 Think of a time you didn't get something you wanted - maybe it was better that way?

🌟 Why would Allah withhold something from us?

🌟 How can you be patient when Allah says "no"?

## How to Use This Beautiful Name

When disappointed: "Allah Al-Qabidh withheld this from me with wisdom. I trust His plan!"

In acceptance: "If Allah withholds something, He knows what's best!"

## Remember:

✨ Allah withholds with perfect wisdom

✨ When Allah says "no," trust Him

✨ Withholding can be a blessing in disguise

✨ Be patient with Allah's decree

grow.title: Al-Basit (The Expander)
grow.content:
### Al Asma ul Husna - 91

## What Does Al-Basit Mean?

Al-Basit means The One Who Expands and Grants Abundance - Allah expands provision and blessings when He wills!

## The Story of Expansion

Fatima's family had very little food one day. They shared what little they had with a poor neighbor.

The next day, unexpectedly, a relative brought lots of groceries!

"Look!" Fatima's mother said. "We gave from our little, and Allah Al-Basit expanded our provision! When Allah wants to give, He gives abundantly!"

"So Allah expanded our food?"

"Yes! Allah Al-Basit can expand anything - provision, knowledge, happiness, blessings!"

## What Can We Learn?

✅ Allah grants abundance - When and how He wills

✅ Allah can expand anything - Provision, blessings, knowledge

✅ Give, and Allah will expand - Generosity brings expansion

✅ Trust Allah's expansion - His giving is perfect

## Activity: Think About It!

🌟 What would you like Allah Al-Basit to expand for you?

🌟 How does giving to others lead to expansion from Allah?

🌟 What blessings has Allah expanded in your life?

## How to Use This Beautiful Name

When asking: "O Allah Al-Basit, please expand my provision and blessings!"

In gratitude: "Alhamdulillah! Allah Al-Basit expanded this for me!"

## Remember:

✨ Allah expands provision and blessings

✨ Generosity brings expansion from Allah

✨ Trust Allah's perfect timing

✨ Al-Qabidh and Al-Basit work together - withholding and expanding with wisdom

grow.title: Al-Muqaddim (Who Brings Forth)
grow.content:
### Al Asma ul Husna - 92

## What Does Al-Muqaddim Mean?

Al-Muqaddim means The One Who Brings Forward - Allah brings people forward in time, status, or priority according to His wisdom!

## The Story of Perfect Timing

In a race, Yusuf was called to the front line even though he signed up late. He won the race!

His coach said, "Sometimes timing matters more than order! And in life, Allah Al-Muqaddim brings forward whoever He wills, whenever He wills!"

"So Allah decided I should go first?"

"Allah brings forward according to His wisdom - sometimes the last becomes first!"

## What Can We Learn?

✅ Allah brings forward whom He wills - In time and status. 

✅ Trust Allah's timing - He knows when to bring things forward 

✅ Don't compete with Allah's decree - He decides what comes first 

✅ Work hard and leave timing to Allah - He'll bring you forward at the right time

## Activity: Think About It!

🌟 When have you been brought forward unexpectedly? That was Allah Al-Muqaddim! 

🌟 Why does Allah bring some things forward and delay others? 

🌟 How can you prepare for when Allah brings you forward?

## How to Use This Beautiful Name

In dua: "O Allah Al-Muqaddim, bring forward what is good for me!"

In patience: "Allah Al-Muqaddim will bring me forward at the right time!"

## Remember:

✨ Allah brings forward according to His wisdom 

✨ Trust Allah's perfect timing 

✨ Prepare yourself for when Allah calls you forward 

✨ The last can become first by Allah's will

grow.title: Al-Muakhkhir (Who Delays Wisely)
grow.content:
### Al Asma ul Husna - 93

## What Does Al-Muakhkhir Mean?

Al-Muakhkhir means The One Who Delays - Allah delays things according to His wisdom, not because He forgot!

## The Story of Delayed Success

Ahmed applied for a special program but wasn't selected. He was disappointed.

A year later, a better program opened up, and Ahmed got in! It was perfect for him!

His father said, "See? Allah Al-Muakhkhir delayed your success because He had something better planned! Allah's delays are not denials - they're redirections to something better!"

## What Can We Learn?

✅ Allah's delays have wisdom - Not because He forgot or doesn't care 

✅ Delays are not denials - Sometimes Allah is preparing something better

✅ Be patient with delays - Trust Allah's timing

✅ What's delayed might be better - Than what came early

## Activity: Think About It!

🌟 What have you been waiting for? Trust Allah Al-Muakhkhir's timing!

🌟 Can you think of a time when a delay turned out to be a blessing? 

🌟 How can you be patient when things are delayed?

## How to Use This Beautiful Name

When waiting: "Allah Al-Muakhkhir delays with wisdom. I will be patient!"

In trust: "If Allah delays it, there's a reason. I trust His plan!"

## Remember:

✨ Allah delays with perfect wisdom 

✨ Delays are not denials 

✨ Be patient - Allah's timing is perfect 

✨ What's delayed may be better for you

grow.title: Al-Muhsin (The Perfecter)
grow.content:
### Al Asma ul Husna - 94

## What Does Al-Muhsin Mean?

Al-Muhsin means The One Who Does Everything Perfectly - Allah does all things with perfection and excellence!

## The Story of Perfect Work

Sara tried her best on her art project, but it still had mistakes.

Her teacher said, "You did your best, and that's wonderful! But remember, only Allah Al-Muhsin does everything perfectly! Every star in the sky is perfectly placed, every snowflake perfectly designed, every baby perfectly formed - that's Allah's perfect work!"

"So I should try to do my best like Allah?"

"Yes! We should always do our best (ihsan), even though only Allah can do things perfectly!"

## What Can We Learn?

✅ Allah does everything perfectly - No mistakes, no flaws 

✅ We should strive for excellence - Doing our best in all things 

✅ Ihsan means excellence - Trying to do things perfectly for Allah 

✅ Appreciate Allah's perfect work - It's all around us

## Activity: Think About It!

🌟 Look around - can you see Allah's perfect work in nature? 

🌟 What does "doing your best" mean? 

🌟 How can you try to be excellent in your work?

## How to Use This Beautiful Name

When doing something: "O Allah Al-Muhsin, help me do this with excellence!"

In appreciation: "Subhanallah! Look at Allah Al-Muhsin's perfect creation!"

## Remember:

✨ Allah does everything perfectly 

✨ We should strive for excellence (ihsan) 

✨ Do your best in everything for Allah 

✨ Appreciate Allah's perfect work all around

grow.title: Al-Muti (The Giver)
grow.content:
### Al Asma ul Husna - 95

## What Does Al-Muti Mean?

Al-Muti means The Giver, The Bestower - Allah gives to whomever He wills, whatever He wills, whenever He wills!

## The Story of The Giver

Little Maryam asked her father, "Why do some people have more and others have less?"

Her father explained, "Allah Al-Muti gives to each person according to His wisdom! He gives some people more wealth, others more health, others more knowledge, others more happiness! Allah is the Giver, and He knows what's best for each person!"

"So Allah decides what to give?"

"Yes! And sometimes what looks like 'less' is actually 'more' in Allah's sight! A little money with peace is better than much money with worry!"

## What Can We Learn?

✅ Allah gives to whom He wills - According to His wisdom 

✅ Everyone gets different gifts - Trust Allah's distribution 

✅ Don't compare - Allah gives each person what's best for them 

✅ Ask Al-Muti to give you - What's best for you

## Activity: Think About It!

🌟 What has Allah Al-Muti given you that others don't have? 

🌟 Why does Allah give different things to different people? 

🌟 Should you be jealous of what others have?

## How to Use This Beautiful Name

When asking: "O Allah Al-Muti, give me what is best for me!"

In contentment: "Allah Al-Muti gave me this, and He knows what's best!"

## Remember:

✨ Allah gives to each according to His wisdom 

✨ Don't compare your gifts with others  

✨ Trust that Allah gives you what's best 

✨ Be content with what Al-Muti has given you

grow.title: Al-Mannan (The Ever-Bestowing)
grow.content:
### Al Asma ul Husna - 96

## What Does Al-Mannan Mean?

Al-Mannan means The Bestower of Blessings - Allah grants favors and blessings continuously without any obligation!

## The Story of Continuous Blessings

Every morning, Bilal would wake up, see the sun, breathe fresh air, and have breakfast.

His grandmother asked, "Who gives you all this every single day?"

"Allah!"

"Yes! Allah Al-Mannan continuously bestows blessings on us! You didn't earn the sunrise, you didn't pay for the air, you didn't create your health - Allah Al-Mannan keeps giving and giving without us even asking!"

"So Allah gives us blessings all the time?"

"Every moment! And He never reminds us 'I gave you this!' - He just keeps giving!"

## What Can We Learn?

✅ Allah continuously bestows blessings - Every moment 

✅ We didn't earn most blessings - Allah gives freely 

✅ Allah never reminds us - "I gave you this!" - Unlike humans 

✅ Be grateful always - For Al-Mannan's continuous gifts

## Activity: Think About It!

🌟 Count 10 blessings you woke up with today - all from Al-Mannan! 

🌟 Did you earn the ability to see, hear, and breathe? No - Allah Al-Mannan gave them freely! 

🌟 How can you show gratitude for continuous blessings?

## How to Use This Beautiful Name

In gratitude: "Alhamdulillah for all the blessings of Allah Al-Mannan!"

When receiving: "This is from Allah Al-Mannan, the Ever-Bestowing!"

## Remember:

✨ Allah bestows blessings continuously 

✨ Most blessings come without us asking 

✨ Allah never reminds us of His favors 

✨ Be grateful for every moment's blessings

grow.title: Al-Witr (The One, The Unique)
grow.content:
### Al Asma ul Husna - 97

## What Does Al-Witr Mean?

Al-Witr means The One, The Unique - Allah is single, unique, and has no equal! Nothing and no one is like Him!

## The Story of The Unique One

In class, teacher showed twins who looked almost identical.

"They look the same!" students said.

"Almost," teacher said. "But look closely - they're still different! However, Allah Al-Witr is absolutely unique! There's nothing even close to being like Him! No second, no copy, no equal!"

"So Allah is completely one of a kind?"

"Yes! Al-Witr means unique and single - there's only ONE Allah, and He's completely unique!"

## What Can We Learn?

✅ Allah is absolutely unique - Nothing is like Him 

✅ Allah is single and alone - No partner, no equal 

✅ Allah loves odd numbers - Including praying Witr prayer 

✅ There's no comparison - Allah is beyond all comparisons

## Activity: Think About It!

🌟 Can you think of anything truly unique? Only Allah is completely unique! 

🌟 What makes Allah so different from everything else? 

🌟 Do you pray Witr prayer? It's named after this beautiful name! 


## How to Use This Beautiful Name

In testimony: "Allah is Al-Witr - completely unique and without equal!"

In prayer: Pray the Witr prayer, named after Allah's uniqueness!

## Remember:

✨ Allah is absolutely unique 

✨ Nothing can be compared to Allah 

✨ Allah is One and Singular 

✨ Allah loves odd numbers and the Witr prayer

grow.title: Conclusion: Living with Allah's Beautiful Names
grow.content:
## Conclusion: Living with Allah's Beautiful Names

Dear children,

You've now learned about 97 of Allah's Beautiful Names! Each name teaches us something amazing about Allah and how we should live.

## Remember These Important Points:

1. **Allah is Perfect** - In every way, with every name
2. **We Should Know Him** - Through His names
3. **We Should Love Him** - Because He is Al-Wadood who loves us
4. **We Should Worship Him** - Because He is Al-Ilah, the only One worthy
5. **We Should Trust Him** - Because He is Al-Wakeel, the best Guardian
6. **We Should Ask Him** - Because He is Al-Mujeeb, who responds
7. **We Should Thank Him** - Because He is Al-Mannan, who continuously gives

## A Special Du'a:

"Allahumma inni as'aluka bi-kulli ismin huwa lak" (O Allah, I ask You by every name that is Yours)

## Your Journey Continues:

* Try to learn one name deeply each week
* See how each name appears in your daily life
* Make dua using Allah's beautiful names
* Try to follow the examples each name teaches us

## The Prophet's Promise:

The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever learns and understands Allah's 99 names will enter Paradise!"

May Allah help us learn His names, understand them, live by them, and enter His Paradise! Ameen!

grow.title: Why Did Allah Create Us? 🌟
grow.content:
## Why Did Allah Create Us? 🌟

Have you ever wondered — why am I here?

It's such an important question. And the amazing thing is — Allah Himself told us the answer in the Quran.

### Allah Tells Us Why

In Surah Al-Mulk, Allah says:

> "He (Allah) created death and life to test you — to see which of you is best in deeds." *(Surah Al-Mulk 67:2)*

Allah created this life as a test. But not a scary test like a hard exam at school. No, no.

It's a test to see: will you try your best? Will you remember Allah? Will you be kind and honest and thankful?

Allah doesn't expect you to be perfect. He just wants to see you try.

### Best — Not Most

Notice something beautiful. Allah didn't say "to see who does the *most* deeds."

He said: "who is *best* in deeds."

That means Allah cares about **how** you do things — not just how many. One small good deed done with love for Allah is better than a hundred deeds done without thinking.

Quality matters more than quantity. Allah sees your heart.

### You Are Not Here by Accident

In the next verse, Allah tells us to look at the sky — the seven heavens He created, one above the other. Perfect. No flaws. No cracks. *(Surah Al-Mulk 67:3)*

If Allah created the sky and the stars with such perfection — do you think He created you without a purpose?

No way.

You are here for a reason. Allah made you to worship Him, to do good, and to earn Jannah — your forever home.

### Things to Remember 💫

- 🤍 Allah created life as a test — a chance to show our goodness.
- 🤍 He wants your best effort, not perfection.
- 🤍 Everything Allah creates has purpose — including YOU.
- 🤍 This life is short. Jannah is forever. So fill your days with good.
- 🤍 Keep trying. Keep coming back to Allah. That's all He asks.

*Ya Allah, help me to do my best for You every single day. Ameen.* 🤍

grow.title: Does Allah Love Me Back? 🥹
grow.content:
## Does Allah Love Me Back? 🥹

Yes. Yes. A thousand times yes.

Allah tells us in the Quran about the people He loves:

- 💚 He loves those who do good — *Al-Muhsineen*
- 💚 He loves those who are patient — *As-Sabireen*
- 💚 He loves those who trust Him — *Al-Mutawakkileen*
- 💚 He loves those who repent — *At-Tawwabeen*
- 💚 He loves those who keep themselves clean and pure — *Al-Mutatahhireen*

You don't have to be perfect. You just have to try.

And when you make mistakes — because everyone does, even grown-ups — just turn back to Allah, say sorry, and try again.

He loves those who come back to Him. He's not angry. He's not tired of you. He's waiting with open arms.

### What Happens When You Love Allah? ✨

When you truly love Allah, something amazing happens inside you.

- 💚 You feel **peaceful** — because you know Allah is in control of everything.
- 💚 You feel **brave** — because you know Allah is protecting you.
- 💚 You feel **grateful** — because you see His blessings everywhere you look.
- 💚 You feel **hopeful** — because you know Allah's mercy is bigger than any problem.
- 💚 You want to **be good** — not to show off, but because you want to please the One you love.

Loving Allah fills your heart in a way that nothing else can. Toys break. Sweets finish. Fun days end. But Allah's love never runs out. Never.

### Things to Remember Every Day 💫

- ✨ Allah made you and He made you special. You are not an accident.
- ✨ Allah hears every prayer. Even the quiet ones. Even the ones without words.
- ✨ Allah is above the heavens — and He is with you through His knowledge, His care, and His love.
- ✨ The more you obey Allah, the closer you feel to Him. Following the Sunnah is the path to Allah's love.
- ✨ You don't need to be perfect. Just keep trying. Keep coming back to Allah.
- ✨ Allah loved you first. Loving Him back is just your heart saying thank you.

*Ya Allah, thank You for loving me before I even knew You. Help me to love You more and more every single day. Ameen.* 🤍

grow.title: How Do I Love Allah? 🤲
grow.content:
## How Do I Love Allah? 🤲

Loving Allah is not just a feeling that stays inside your heart. Real love shows. It shows in what you say. It shows in what you do. It shows in the little choices you make every single day.

So how can you show Allah that you love Him?

### 1. Worship Only Allah

This is the most important thing of all. You pray to Allah alone. You ask help from Allah alone. You don't pray to anyone else — not to angels, not to prophets, not to any person, alive or dead. Only Allah. This is **Tawhid** — and it is the foundation of everything.

### 2. Obey Allah and His Messenger ﷺ

When you love someone, you listen to them, right? If your parents say "don't touch the stove," you listen because you trust them.

Allah's rules are the same. They protect you. They guide you to what's best. And the Prophet ﷺ showed us exactly how to follow Allah's guidance.

> "Say, if you love Allah, then follow me (the Prophet), and Allah will love you." *(Surah Aal-Imran 3:31)*

How beautiful is that? When you follow the Prophet ﷺ, **Allah loves you back**!

### 3. Remember Allah A Lot

Talk to Allah during your day. Not just during prayer — all day long. Say *"Bismillah"* before you eat. Say *"Alhamdulillah"* when something good happens. Say *"SubhanAllah"* when you see something amazing.

These little words are like seeds you plant in your heart. They keep Allah with you all day long.

### 4. Pray Your Salah With Your Heart

When you stand in prayer, you are standing in front of Allah — the King of everything. And He is listening to you. Just you.

Try to think about what you're saying. Even if you don't understand all the words yet — know this: you are talking to the One who loves you most.

### 5. Make Dua — Talk to Allah Anytime

You don't need a special time or place. Tell Him what makes you happy. Tell Him what scares you. Ask Him for help. Thank Him for everything.

He loves to hear from you. He really, truly does.

### 6. Learn About Allah

The more you know about Allah, the more you will love Him. Learn His beautiful names. Read the Quran. Listen to stories about the Prophet ﷺ.

When you understand who Allah really is — how kind, how merciful, how great He is — your heart can't help but fill with love.

### 7. Love What Allah Loves

- Allah loves **kindness** — so be kind.
- Allah loves **honesty** — so tell the truth.
- Allah loves **patience** — so try to be patient.
- Allah loves **those who help others** — so look for ways to help.

### 8. Stay Away From What Allah Doesn't Like

If you love someone, you don't want to upset them. Allah doesn't like lying, hurting others, meanness, or pride. So try your best to avoid these — not because you're scared, but because you love Allah.

### Things to Remember 💫

- 🤍 Loving Allah isn't just a feeling — it's shown through your actions.
- 🤍 Tawhid comes first. Pray to Allah alone. Ask from Allah alone.
- 🤍 Following the Prophet ﷺ is the key to Allah's love.
- 🤍 Little words like Bismillah and Alhamdulillah keep Allah in your heart all day.
- 🤍 You can talk to Allah anytime, anywhere. He is never too busy for you.
- 🤍 The more you learn about Allah, the more your love will grow.

*Ya Allah, help me to love You with my whole heart — and to show that love in everything I say and do. Ameen.* 🤍

grow.title: Why Should I Love Allah? 💚
grow.content:
## Why Should I Love Allah? 💚

Think about everyone who has ever been kind to you. Your parents who tuck you in at night. Your grandparents who tell you stories. Your teachers who help you learn. Your friends who make you laugh.

Now think about this: **every single good thing you have ever received came from Allah.**

Your family? Allah gave them to you. Your home? From Allah. Your food? From Allah. Your health? From Allah. The air you breathe? From Allah.

Every smile. Every happy moment. Every blessing you can think of — all from Him.

### Gifts Beyond Counting

If someone gave you one gift, you would love them, right? You would say thank you and feel happy inside.

But Allah has given you **thousands and thousands** of gifts. Gifts you can count — and gifts you cannot even see. Gifts you know about — and gifts you don't even realize are there.

### The Greatest Gift of All

And there's more. Allah also **guides** you. He didn't leave you confused about how to live. He didn't let you wander around lost and alone.

He sent the **Quran** — His perfect words. And He sent **Prophet Muhammad ﷺ** — to show you exactly how to walk this path.

That's the biggest gift of all.

### The Most Natural Thing

So loving Allah isn't hard when you really think about it. It isn't something you have to force or pretend.

He loved you first. He gave you everything first. He cared for you before you even knew His name.

Loving Him back? That's just the most natural thing your heart can do.

### Things to Remember 💫

- 🤍 Every good thing in your life is a gift from Allah — every single one.
- 🤍 Allah didn't just create you and leave you. He sent guidance so you would never be lost.
- 🤍 You don't have to search for reasons to love Allah. Just look around you — the reasons are everywhere.
- 🤍 Allah loved you first. Loving Him back is simply your heart saying thank you.
- 🤍 The more you notice Allah's gifts, the more your love for Him will grow.

*Ya Allah, thank You for every blessing You have given me — the ones I see and the ones I don't. Help my heart to always remember Your kindness and to love You more each day. Ameen.* 🤍

grow.title: What Is Allah Like? ✨
grow.content:
## What Is Allah Like? ✨

How do we know what Allah is like?

Allah told us about Himself in the Quran. And Prophet Muhammad ﷺ taught us too. We believe exactly what they told us — no more, no less. We don't make things up or guess. We simply trust what Allah and His Messenger ﷺ said.

And what they told us is so, so beautiful. Allah has many names — **99 beautiful names** — and each one tells us something amazing about who He is.

### Ar-Rahman & Ar-Raheem — The Most Merciful

Allah's mercy is bigger than anything you can ever imagine. Bigger than the sky. Bigger than the ocean. Bigger than the whole universe.

You know how your mother loves you? How she takes care of you when you're sick, hugs you when you're sad, and forgives you when you make mistakes?

**Allah told us that He is even more merciful to you than your own mother.**

Even when you do something wrong, Allah doesn't want to punish you — He wants to forgive you. He's just waiting for you to say sorry and come back to Him.

### Al-Khaliq — The Creator 🌸

Look around you. The tall mountains. The tiny ants. The bright sun. The soft rain.

Allah created all of it. Every leaf. Every drop. Every star. And out of all His creations — He made **YOU**. That means you are special to Him.

### As-Samee' — The All-Hearing 👂

Allah hears everything. When you whisper a little prayer at night under your blanket, He hears it. When you're sad and your heart is hurting inside, He knows. When you say *"Alhamdulillah"* so quietly that no one else can hear — Allah hears every letter.

You never have to shout for Allah to hear you. He's always listening — always.

### Al-Baseer — The All-Seeing 👁️

Allah sees everything. He sees when you share your snack even though you wanted it all. He sees when you help your mama without being asked. He sees when you're kind to someone and nobody notices.

Even when no one else is watching — **Allah is watching**. And He sees your kindness, your effort, your good heart. Nothing good you do is ever missed.

### Al-Wadud — The Most Loving 💚

Allah loves. And He loves to be loved. He loves those who do good, those who are patient, those who trust Him, those who come back to Him again and again.

And He doesn't just love — He wants **you** to love Him back. The Creator of everything wants your little heart to love Him. And when you do, He draws even closer to you.

### Al-Qareeb — The Near One 🤲

Even though Allah is above the heavens, above His mighty Throne — He is never far from you. When you call upon Him, He hears you right away. Just close your eyes, raise your hands, and talk to Him.

He is near. Always near.

These are just a few of Allah's beautiful names. But even these few are enough to make your heart feel full. Because when you know who Allah is — how merciful, how loving, how close He is — you can't help but love Him.

And the best part? **He already loves you.** 💚

grow.title: Who Is Allah?
grow.content:
## Who Is Allah? 🤍

**Allah is your Creator.**

He made you. He made your eyes that see beautiful colors. He made your ears that hear your mama's voice. He made your heart that beats and beats without you even thinking about it.

Before you were born — before you took your very first breath — Allah already knew you. He planned every little thing about you. The color of your eyes. The sound of your laugh. The way you smile. And He made you just right.

### Allah is the One and Only God

There is nothing like Him — nothing in the sky, nothing on the earth, nothing anywhere. He doesn't have parents or children. He wasn't born and He will never die. He has always been there, and He will always be there. He is perfect in every single way.

This is called **Tawhid** — believing that Allah alone is God, and only He deserves to be worshipped. No one else. Just Him.

### Where Is Allah?

The Quran and the Prophet ﷺ taught us clearly that **Allah is above the heavens, above His Throne (Al-Arsh)**. This is what the early Muslims — the Salaf — believed, and we believe exactly the same.

But here's something wonderful: even though Allah is high above everything, **He sees you. He hears you. He knows everything about you** — your thoughts, your feelings, your dreams, your worries. Nothing is hidden from Him.

Allah is with you through His knowledge, His care, and His protection — wherever you are, whatever you're doing.

Have you noticed that when you raise your hands to make dua, you naturally look up? That's because your heart knows. Your heart knows that Allah is above, watching over you with love and mercy.

So remember: the One who made the stars and the oceans and the mountains — that same Allah made **YOU**. And He is always near, always listening, always caring for you. 💚

grow.title: I am a Muslim
grow.content:
## What Does It Mean to Be a Muslim?

Being a Muslim means you believe in one God — Allah — and you try your best to be a good person every single day.

The word "Muslim" actually means someone who listens to Allah and follows His guidance. It's like having the best teacher in the whole universe showing you the right way to live!

### Why Should You Feel Happy About Being Muslim?

## 1. You Have the Best Gift Ever!
Being a Muslim is a special gift from Allah. It's not because we're smarter or better than anyone else — it's because Allah chose to guide us. And for that, we say "Alhamdulillah" (which means "Thank you, Allah!").

## 2. You Follow the Best Examples

A long, long time ago, there were very good Muslims who lived right after Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. They were called the Salaf al-Salih — which means "the good people who came before us." They showed us exactly how to be great Muslims, and we get to learn from them!

## 3. You Have a Superpower Called Tawhid

Tawhid means believing that Allah is the ONE and ONLY God. There's no one like Him. He created everything — the stars, the oceans, the animals, and YOU! When you remember this, you feel strong because you know the Creator of everything loves you and is always with you.

## 4. You Have a Guidebook for Life

Imagine having a perfect instruction book that tells you how to be happy, how to treat people, and how to solve any problem. That's what the Quran and the teachings of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ (called the Sunnah) are! They help you know what to do in every situation.

## 5. You Belong to a Huge Family
There are Muslims all around the world — in every country, speaking different languages, eating different foods — but all of them are your brothers and sisters in faith. How cool is that?

## What's the Difference Between Good Pride and Bad Pride?

This is really important to understand!

Good pride is feeling happy and grateful that Allah guided you. It makes you want to be even kinder, more helpful, and closer to Allah.

Bad pride (called kibr in Arabic) is when someone thinks they're better than other people. This is a big mistake that Allah doesn't like.

So remember: Be thankful, not boastful!

## Things to Remember Every Day 💫

✨ Say "Alhamdulillah" a lot! When you wake up, when you eat, when something good happens — thank Allah!

✨ Allah is always with you. When you're scared, happy, sad, or confused — talk to Him. He always listens.

✨ Be kind to EVERYONE. Muslims and non-Muslims, friends and strangers, people and animals too!

✨ Try your best, but don't worry about being perfect. Allah knows you're trying, and He loves that.

✨ Learn a little bit every day. Maybe one small thing about how the Prophet ﷺ lived. Small steps lead to big changes!

## Your Little To-Do List ✅

Here are some simple things you can start doing:

- Morning: When you wake up, say "Alhamdulillah" and thank Allah for a new day
- Be Helpful: Do one kind thing today without anyone asking you
- Tell the Truth: Even when it's hard, be honest
- Pray: Talk to Allah in your prayers and really mean it
- Learn: Ask a parent or teacher to tell you one story about the Prophet ﷺ or his companions
- Bedtime: Before you sleep, think of three things you're thankful for


## A Special Reminder Just for You 🤲

Being Muslim isn't about being perfect. It's about trying your best and knowing that Allah sees your effort.

When you make mistakes (and everyone does!), just say sorry to Allah, try to do better, and move on. Allah is the Most Merciful — He loves to forgive.

You are special. You are loved. And you have the most beautiful gift in the world — the gift of Islam.

So smile, be grateful, and shine your light wherever you go!

grow.title: The Five Pillars of Islam
grow.content:
### What Are the Five Pillars of Islam?

Hello, young friends! Today we're going to learn about something very special in Islam called the "Five Pillars."

What's a pillar? Think about a big, strong building. What holds it up? Pillars! They're like tall, strong columns that keep the building standing straight and tall.

In Islam, there are five important things that Muslims do to make their faith strong, just like pillars hold up a building. These are called the Five Pillars of Islam.

### The Five Pillars Are:

- Shahadah - Believing and saying what you believe
- Salah - Praying five times every day
- Zakah - Sharing with people who need help
- Sawm - Fasting during the month of Ramadan
- Hajj - Visiting the holy city of Makkah

### Why Are They Important?

These five pillars help Muslims:

- Stay close to Allah (God)
- Be kind and caring to others
- Become better people
- Feel connected to Muslims all around the world
- Live a happy and peaceful life

Think of it this way: If you want to be good at something, you practice, right? If you want to be good at soccer, you practice kicking the ball. If you want to be good at reading, you practice reading books. The Five Pillars are like practice for being a good Muslim and a good person!

grow.title: Shahadah
grow.content:
### What Is Shahadah?

Shahadah is a special sentence that Muslims say and believe in their hearts. It goes like this:

"There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is His messenger."

This is the very first pillar of Islam, and it's the most important one! It's like the foundation of a house - everything else is built on top of it.

### What Does It Mean?

Let's break it down into two parts:

## Part 1: "There is no god but Allah"

This means Muslims believe that Allah is the one and only God. Allah created everything we see:

- The bright sun and shining moon
- All the stars in the sky
- Mountains, oceans, and rivers
- Every animal, bird, and fish
- All people in the world
- You and me!

Allah is the most powerful, the most kind, and the most wise. He takes care of everything.

## Part 2: "Muhammad is His messenger"

This means Muslims believe that Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was a special teacher sent by Allah. He taught people how to live good lives and how to worship Allah in the right way.

Think of it like this: If Allah sent you a letter, Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was the messenger who delivered it and explained it to everyone!

### How Do Muslims Show This Belief?

Muslims show they believe by:

- Saying the Shahadah out loud
- Loving Allah and trying to make Him happy
- Following the teachings of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)
- Being thankful for all the good things Allah gives them
- Worshipping only Allah and no one else

### Why Is Shahadah So Important?

Shahadah is like a key that opens the door to Islam! When someone says the Shahadah and truly believes it in their heart, they become a Muslim.

It reminds Muslims:

- Who created them and takes care of them
- That Allah is always watching and knows everything
- To be good people because Allah wants them to be kind and honest
- That Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) showed them the best way to live

### A Story to Remember

Imagine you have a best friend. How do people know you're best friends? You say it! You spend time together, you help each other, and you show you care. Shahadah is like telling everyone, "Allah is my God, and I believe in His messenger!" Then Muslims show it through their actions every single day.

Remember!

The Shahadah is:

- The first and most important pillar
- A statement of belief in Allah and His messenger
- The foundation for all other pillars
- Something Muslims carry in their hearts always

grow.title: Salah (Prayer)
grow.content:
## What Is Salah?

Salah means **prayer**. It's how Muslims talk to Allah **five times every single day**! Just like you might talk to your parents when you need something or want to say thank you, Muslims talk to Allah through prayer.

### The Five Daily Prayers

- **Fajr** ☀️ — Early morning, before the sun comes up
- **Zuhr** 🌤️ — Middle of the day, just after noon
- **Asr** 🌅 — Afternoon time
- **Maghrib** 🌆 — Right after the sun sets
- **Isha** 🌙 — At night when it gets dark

No matter where Muslims are in the world — at home, at school, or traveling — they stop and pray at these times!

### How Do Muslims Pray?

When Muslims pray, they:
- **Face toward the Kaaba** in Makkah (a special holy place)
- **Stand, bow, and put their forehead on the ground**
- **Say special words** praising Allah
- Make sure they're **clean and wearing modest clothes**

It's like having a special meeting with Allah five times a day!

### What Do Muslims Say in Prayer?

During prayer, Muslims:
- **Thank** Allah for all the good things they have
- **Ask** Allah for help with their problems
- **Say sorry** for any mistakes they made
- **Ask** Allah to bless their family and friends
- **Praise** Allah for being so great and kind

### Why Do Muslims Pray Five Times a Day?

**1. To Remember Allah** — Life gets busy! Prayer reminds Muslims to stop and think about Allah throughout the day.

**2. To Say Thank You** — Allah gives us so many things. Prayer is a time to say "Thank you, Allah!"

**3. To Ask for Help** — Everyone needs help sometimes. Muslims can ask Allah for anything — big or small.

**4. To Become Better People** — When you remember Allah and talk to Him every day, you want to be a good person!

**5. To Feel Peaceful** — Prayer is like a calm, quiet time. It helps Muslims feel peaceful and happy inside.

### Special Things About Prayer

- **Prayer washes away mistakes** — The Prophet ﷺ said praying five times a day is like bathing in a clean river five times — it washes away all the dirt!
- **Praying together is extra special** — At the mosque, it's **27 times better** than praying alone!
- **Prayer brings you closer to Allah** — It's like a special call to Allah that's always available

### Remember!

- Muslims pray five times every day
- Prayer is talking to Allah
- It helps Muslims feel peaceful and become better people
- Prayer washes away small mistakes
- It's like a special meeting with Allah!

grow.title: Zakah (Sharing with Those in Need)
grow.content:
## What Is Zakah?

Zakah means **giving money or things to help poor people**. It's a special kind of sharing that Allah asks Muslims to do every year.

Think of it like this: when you have extra cookies and your friend has none, what do you do? You share! Zakah is Muslims sharing their money with people who don't have enough.

### Why Did Allah Create Rich and Poor People?

Allah made some people rich and some people poor for a special reason. He wants to see:
- Will rich people be **kind and share**?
- Will poor people be **patient and grateful**?

It's like a test to see if we have good hearts!

### Who Gives Zakah?

Muslims who have enough money saved up for one whole year must give some of it away.

**How much?** About **2.5%** of their savings. That means if someone has 100 dollars saved, they give 2.50 dollars. It's a small amount, but when many people give together, it helps a lot!

Children, poor people, and those without extra money don't have to give zakah. But they can still give other small gifts (called **sadaqah**) when they want to help!

### Who Receives Zakah?

- Poor people who don't have enough food
- People who don't have homes
- People who can't pay their bills
- Travelers who ran out of money
- People working to teach others about Islam

### Why Is Zakah Important?

**It Helps Poor People** — You help someone buy food, get clothes, or have a place to sleep.

**It Makes Your Heart Better** — Sharing removes greedy feelings. You learn to be happy with what you have.

**It Creates Love** — When rich people help poor people, everyone loves each other more. Everyone feels like one big, caring family!

**It Makes Communities Stronger** — Imagine if everyone in your neighborhood helped each other. That's what zakah does.

**It Brings Blessings** — Allah promises that when you give zakah, He will bless the money you keep!

### The Beautiful Side of Giving

Here's something cool: it's actually better to give zakah **quietly**! Allah loves it when people help others without showing off.

The Prophet ﷺ taught that the best giving is when your left hand doesn't know what your right hand gave. That means you give so quietly that even you almost forget about it!

### Remember!

- Zakah means sharing money with people in need
- Muslims with extra money give about 2.5% each year
- It helps poor people and makes communities stronger
- Giving removes greedy feelings and creates love
- It's best to give quietly without showing off
- Allah blesses those who share!

grow.title: Sawm (Fasting During Ramadan)
grow.content:
## What Is Sawm?

Sawm means **fasting** — not eating or drinking during the daytime for one whole month called **Ramadan**.

Muslims wake up very early before the sun comes up to eat breakfast (called **Suhoor**). Then they don't eat or drink anything — not even water! — until the sun goes down. When the sun sets, they break their fast with a meal called **Iftar**.

They do this every single day for one month!

### What Is Ramadan?

Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar. It's super special because:
- The **Quran** was first revealed during this month
- Good deeds count **extra** during Ramadan
- There's a special night called **Laylat al-Qadr** that's better than 1,000 months!
- Families and friends come together more
- Everyone tries extra hard to be good people

### Who Has to Fast?

**Must fast:** Adult Muslims who are healthy and able
**Don't have to fast:** Young children, elderly, sick people, pregnant women, and travelers

Allah is very kind and understanding. He doesn't want anyone to get sick or hurt!

### Why Do Muslims Fast?

**1. To Feel What Hungry People Feel**
When you don't eat all day, you understand how poor people feel. This makes you want to help them more!

**2. To Practice Self-Control**
If you can say "no" to food when you're hungry, you can say "no" to other bad things too.

**3. To Become More Patient**
Going without food is hard! But it teaches you patience that helps in all parts of life.

**4. To Get Closer to Allah**
When you're fasting, you think about Allah more, pray more, and try harder to be good.

**5. To Appreciate What You Have**
When you finally eat after fasting, food tastes amazing! You realize how lucky you are.

### Special Ramadan Moments

**Suhoor** — Families wake up together while it's still dark. Quiet and peaceful.

**Iftar** — Muslims eat dates and drink water first (like the Prophet ﷺ), then pray, then have a big meal together. It's like a daily celebration!

**Laylat al-Qadr** — The most special night of the year! One night better than **1,000 months**! Muslims stay up praying and asking Allah for forgiveness.

**Eid al-Fitr** — When Ramadan ends, there's a huge celebration! Everyone wears nice clothes, families visit each other, kids get gifts, and everyone eats delicious food together.

### Remember!

- Sawm means fasting during Ramadan
- Muslims don't eat or drink from sunrise to sunset
- It teaches patience, self-control, and gratitude
- Not everyone has to fast — Allah is kind and understanding
- It ends with a big celebration called Eid!

grow.title: Hajj
grow.content:
## What Is Hajj?

Hajj is a special journey that Muslims take to Makkah, the holiest city in Islam. It's like the biggest family reunion in the world, where millions of Muslims from every country come together!

### What Is the Kaaba?

In Makkah, there's a very special building called the **Kaaba**. It looks like a big black cube covered with a beautiful cloth.

The Kaaba is super important because:
- It's the **first house built** to worship Allah
- Muslims all over the world **face toward it** when they pray
- Prophet Ibrahim and his son Ismail **built it** thousands of years ago

When Muslims go for Hajj, they visit the Kaaba and walk around it **seven times**!

### Who Goes for Hajj?

Every Muslim who can afford it and is healthy enough should try to go **at least once** in their lifetime. You don't have to go if you're too young, sick, or don't have enough money. Allah only asks people to do what they're able to do.

### When Is Hajj?

Hajj happens during specific days in the **12th month** of the Islamic calendar (Dhul-Hijjah). Every year, about 2-3 million Muslims travel to Makkah at the same time!

### What Do People Do During Hajj?

**1. Wearing Special Clothes (Ihram)**
Men wear two simple white sheets. Everyone looks the same! You can't tell who's rich or poor. Everyone is **equal** before Allah.

**2. Walking Around the Kaaba (Tawaf)**
Muslims walk around the Kaaba **seven times**, praying and remembering Allah.

**3. Walking Between Two Hills (Sa'i)**
They walk back and forth seven times between Safa and Marwa — remembering Hajar searching for water for her baby.

**4. Standing at Arafat**
This is the **most important part**! All pilgrims stand on a plain called Arafat, praying to Allah from noon until sunset.

**5. Throwing Pebbles**
Muslims throw small stones at three pillars — remembering Prophet Ibrahim rejecting the devil's temptations.

**6. Celebrating Eid al-Adha**
Families sacrifice an animal and share the meat with poor people, remembering Prophet Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice for Allah.

### Why Is Hajj So Special?

- **It shows we're all equal** — rich or poor, everyone wears the same clothes
- **It brings Muslims together** — people from every country, united by love for Allah
- **It's like pressing the reset button** — the Prophet ﷺ said you come back as clean from sins as the day you were born!
- **It teaches patience** — because it's hard work!
- **It's a practice** for the Day of Judgment — when everyone will stand before Allah

### Remember!

- Hajj is a journey to Makkah, the holiest city in Islam
- Muslims visit the Kaaba and do special acts of worship
- Everyone wears simple clothes to show they're equal
- Millions of Muslims from all over the world go together
- Hajj washes away sins and makes you a better person!

grow.title: The Two Magic Words - Bismillah!
grow.content:
## The Two Magic Words - Bismillah!

Do you know the most powerful words you can say before doing anything? Just two simple words: **Bismillah** - "In the name of Allah."

These aren't just ordinary words. They're like a key that unlocks Allah's blessings and barakah (goodness) in everything you do!

### The Missing Key to Blessings

Imagine you're about to start eating, studying for a test, playing a game, or even going to sleep. What if I told you that saying one simple phrase could bring Allah's blessings into that moment? That's exactly what Bismillah does!

The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) taught us in an authentic hadith: **"Any important matter that does not begin with 'Bismillah' is cut off (from blessings)."** (Abu Dawud)

Think about it - "cut off from blessings" means you're missing out on something amazing! It's like having a treasure chest right in front of you but forgetting the key. Bismillah is that key!

### Your Invisible Shield

Here's something that will blow your mind. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said in Sahih Muslim: **"When a person enters his home and mentions Allah's name when entering and while eating, Satan says: 'You have no place to stay and no meal.' But when he enters without mentioning Allah's name, Satan says: 'You have found a place to stay,' and when he does not mention Allah's name while eating, Satan says: 'You have found a place to stay and a meal.'"**

Whoa! So saying Bismillah actually keeps Shaytan away from you! It's like an invisible shield of protection. When you say it, Shaytan can't mess with what you're doing.

### What Bismillah Really Means

When you say Bismillah, you're having a conversation with Allah. You're saying:

*"O Allah, I'm about to do this, and I can't do it without You. Please be with me. Please bless it. Please make it good. I'm starting this in YOUR name, not my own."*

That's love. That's trust. That's faith.

Imam Ibn al-Qayyim, one of the greatest Islamic scholars, beautifully explained: **"Bismillah is like planting your action in blessed soil. Without it, your action is like a seed thrown on barren ground."**

He meant that when you say Bismillah:
- You're remembering Allah is with you
- You're asking for His help
- You're admitting you can't do anything without Him
- You're inviting His blessings into your life

### Start Today!

For today, try saying Bismillah before just THREE things:
1. Before you eat
2. Before you study or do homework
3. Before you go to sleep

Notice how it feels. Notice how it makes you think of Allah. That's the beginning of a beautiful habit!

**Remember:** Even the smallest action becomes special when you begin it with Allah's name. That's the power of Bismillah! 💚

---

### References

**Authentic Hadith:**
- Sunan Abu Dawud, Book 34 (General Behavior), Hadith 4840 - "Any important matter that does not begin with 'Bismillah' is cut off (from blessings)"
- Sahih Muslim, Book 36 (The Book of Drinks), Hadith 2018 - "When a person enters his home and mentions Allah's name when entering and while eating, Satan says: 'You have no place to stay and no meal.' But when he enters without mentioning Allah's name, Satan says: 'You have found a place to stay,' and when he does not mention Allah's name while eating, Satan says: 'You have found a place to stay and a meal'"

**Scholars:**
- Imam Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah (1292-1350 CE) - On the blessing of beginning actions with Bismillah

grow.title: Even Kings Say Bismillah!
grow.content:
## Even Kings Say Bismillah!

### The Letter from a Powerful King

Do you remember Prophet Sulaiman (peace be upon him)? Allah gave him an incredible kingdom - he could talk to animals, control the wind, and command the jinn! He was one of the most powerful people to ever live.

But look at what he said in the Quran when he wrote a letter:

**"Indeed, it is from Sulaiman, and indeed, it is 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.'"** (Quran 27:30)

Even though Sulaiman was a mighty king with superpowers, he started his letter with Bismillah! He didn't start with "I am the great King Sulaiman" or "Look at how powerful I am!" 

No - he started with Allah's name.

That's humility. That's wisdom. That's how the righteous people lived.

### The Scholar Who Never Forgot

**Imam Ahmad's Beautiful Habit**

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal was one of the greatest scholars in Islamic history. Do you know what made him even more special? He would say Bismillah before EVERYTHING - even before tying his shoelaces!

His students asked him, "Teacher, why even for small things?" 

He smiled and said, **"How can I call anything small when it involves the name of Allah? Everything becomes great when done with His name."**

Think about that. Tying your shoes becomes an act of worship when you say Bismillah. Playing with your friends becomes blessed when you say Bismillah. Everything changes!

### The Writing Lesson

Shaykh Ibn Taymiyyah used to tell his students this story:

A man was writing and making mistakes over and over. He kept erasing and rewriting, getting more and more frustrated. His paper was a mess!

A wise scholar passed by and asked, "Did you say Bismillah before you started?"

The man's face went red. He had forgotten! 

He said Bismillah, started again with a fresh paper, and this time the words flowed perfectly. No mistakes!

The scholar told him something beautiful: **"When you begin with Allah's name, He helps you. When you begin without it, you're on your own."**

### The Question That Changes Everything

Here's something to think about: If the greatest kings, the smartest scholars, and the most righteous people all said Bismillah before everything they did... shouldn't we?

They had so much knowledge, so much power, so much talent. But they knew a secret: **All of it came from Allah.** Without His help, without His blessings, nothing would work.

That's why they never forgot to say Bismillah.

### Your Turn to Be Great

When you say Bismillah, you're following in the footsteps of prophets, scholars, and the best people who ever lived. You're joining them in remembering Allah before every action.

And here's the beautiful part: You don't have to be a king or a scholar to do this. You just have to remember. You just have to care. You just have to say those two simple, powerful words.

**Try this challenge:** Tomorrow, say Bismillah before three NEW things you don't usually say it for:
- Before leaving your house
- Before opening a book
- Before drinking water

Watch how it makes you feel more connected to Allah! 💫

---

### References

**Quran:**
- Surah An-Naml (27:30) - "Indeed, it is from Sulaiman, and indeed, it is 'In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful'"

**Scholars:**
- Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal (780-855 CE) - His practice of saying Bismillah before every action, narrated by his students in biographical accounts
- Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (1263-1328 CE) - Stories and teachings from his lectures to students about the importance of Bismillah

grow.title: When You Forget Bismillah
grow.content:
## When You Forget Bismillah

### It Happens to Everyone

You sit down to eat. You take a big bite. And then... oh no! You forgot to say Bismillah!

Your heart sinks a little. You feel bad. But guess what? Don't worry at all! Allah is so kind and merciful that He gave us a beautiful solution.

### The Second-Chance Du'a

The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) taught us something amazing in an authentic hadith. If you forget to say Bismillah at the beginning, you can say:

**"Bismillah awwalahu wa akhirahu"**
(In the name of Allah at its beginning and at its end)

Isn't that beautiful? Allah doesn't want you to feel guilty or sad. He gives you another chance! You can say Bismillah in the middle, at the end - anytime you remember!

This shows us how merciful Allah is. He knows we're human. He knows we forget. And He loves when we come back to Him, even if we started without remembering.

### The Amazing Promise

Here's something that might make you cry happy tears. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said in Sahih Bukhari: 

**"Whoever eats food and then says: 'Praise be to Allah who has fed me this and provided it for me without any power or might on my part,' his previous sins will be forgiven."**

Just imagine - remembering Allah and thanking Him can erase sins! How incredibly merciful is our Lord?

### Small Words, Huge Impact

Sometimes we think, "It's just two words. How important can they be?"

But think about this: When you press a light switch, it's just a tiny movement of your finger, right? But that tiny movement lights up an entire room!

Bismillah is like that. It's small to say, but it lights up your entire action with Allah's blessings.

Shaykh Abdul Aziz ibn Baz, a great scholar, used to say: **"The person who constantly says Bismillah lives a life of awareness. They know Allah is watching, helping, and blessing them. How can such a person ever feel alone or hopeless?"**

### The Life-Changing Habit

Imagine living every single day knowing that Allah is with you in everything you do. That's what Bismillah gives you!

When you say it before eating - Allah blesses your food.
When you say it before studying - Allah helps you understand.
When you say it before sleeping - Allah protects you through the night.

It's like having the Creator of the Universe as your helper, your protector, your friend - in every single moment!

### Your Promise to Yourself

Here's a challenge: For the next three days, every time you remember, say Bismillah. Don't beat yourself up when you forget - just say it when you remember!

Keep count in your head or on paper. How many times can you remember to say Bismillah in one day? 

10 times? 20 times? 50 times?

Each time you say it, you're:
- ✨ Remembering Allah
- ✨ Earning rewards
- ✨ Getting blessings
- ✨ Protecting yourself from Shaytan
- ✨ Making your action better

That's a lot of good from just two words!

**Remember:** Allah loves consistency, even if it's small. It's better to say Bismillah sometimes and keep trying than to never say it at all. Start where you are, and grow from there! 🌱

---

### References

**Authentic Hadith:**
- Sunan Abu Dawud, Book 27 (Foods), Hadith 3767 - "When any of you eats, let him mention the name of Allah. If he forgets to mention the name of Allah at the beginning, let him say: 'Bismillah awwalahu wa akhirahu' (In the name of Allah at its beginning and at its end)"
- Sunan At-Tirmidhi, Book 48 (Supplications), Hadith 3458 - Similar narration about saying Bismillah when you remember
- Sahih Bukhari, Book 80 (Invocations), Hadith 6086 - "Whoever eats food and then says: 'Praise be to Allah who has fed me this and provided it for me without any power or might on my part,' his previous sins will be forgiven"

**Scholars:**
- Shaykh Abdul Aziz ibn Baz (1910-1999 CE) - From his various lectures and fatwas on the importance of dhikr and remembrance of Allah

grow.title: Allah Remembers You Back
grow.content:
## Allah Remembers You Back

### The Most Beautiful Promise

The Quran tells us something that should make our hearts melt:

**"So remember Me; I will remember you."** (Quran 2:152)

Let that sink in for a moment. When you say Bismillah - when you remember Allah - He remembers you back.

Think about it: The Creator of the stars, the oceans, the mountains, the entire universe... He remembers little you. Every. Single. Time. You. Say. His. Name.

Can you imagine? 

Out of billions of people, trillions of angels, countless creatures - when YOU say "Bismillah," Allah knows. Allah hears. Allah remembers you.

### The Story You'll Never Forget

Here's something that might make you emotional:

One day, years from now, you'll be older. Maybe you'll face something difficult - a hard test, a scary situation, or a sad moment.

And without even thinking about it, your tongue will automatically say "Bismillah."

Your heart will feel calm. Your worries will feel lighter. And you'll realize something beautiful:

All those times you practiced saying Bismillah as a kid? They weren't just words. They were building something inside you. They were teaching your heart to always run to Allah first.

That's when you'll understand: Allah was preparing you all along. Every Bismillah was a seed, and now you're seeing the tree it grew into.

### Living with Bismillah

When you fill your life with Bismillah, everything changes:

**Your morning changes** - You wake up saying Bismillah, knowing Allah is with you for the new day.

**Your food changes** - Every meal becomes blessed, every bite thanking Allah.

**Your work changes** - Homework isn't boring anymore; it's something you're doing with Allah's help.

**Your play changes** - Even fun becomes worship when you start it with Allah's name.

**Your sleep changes** - You close your eyes peacefully, knowing Allah is protecting you.

That's not just living. That's living with PURPOSE. That's living with MEANING. That's living with ALLAH.

### Your Life Starts with Bismillah

Here's the beautiful truth: A life filled with Bismillah is a life filled with blessings. 

Never underestimate these two small words. They connect your heart to the Heavens. They turn ordinary moments into worship. They make everything you do - no matter how small - special in the sight of Allah.

Remember what we learned:
- Bismillah brings blessings to everything you do
- It protects you from Shaytan
- Prophets and scholars never forgot it
- Even if you forget, you can say it anytime
- When you remember Allah, He remembers you

### Begin Right Now

Close your eyes for just a moment. 

Say "Bismillah" - but this time, say it with your heart, not just your tongue. 

Feel what it means. You're calling upon the Most Powerful, the Most Loving, the One who created you and knows you better than you know yourself.

Now open your eyes. 

Say Bismillah. 

And begin.

Begin your kindness. Begin your journey to become better. Begin with Allah's name, and watch how He puts barakah in every step you take.

**Bismillah.**

That's where all good things begin. 💚

---

*May Allah bless every child who reads this and fills their life with His beautiful remembrance. May you grow up always remembering Him, and may He always be with you. Ameen.* 🤲

---

### References

**Quran:**
- Surah Al-Baqarah (2:152) - "So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me"
- Surah Al-Fatiha (1:1) - "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" - The opening of the Quran begins with Bismillah
- Surah An-Naml (27:30) - Prophet Sulaiman's letter beginning with Bismillah

**Authentic Hadith:**
- Sahih Bukhari, Book 97 (Oneness of Allah), Hadith 7405 - Hadith Qudsi: "I am as My servant thinks I am, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself; and if he remembers Me in a group of people, I remember him in a group that is better than them"
- Sahih Muslim, Book 48 (The Book of Dhikr), Hadith 2675 - Similar narration about Allah remembering those who remember Him

grow.title: Alhamdulillah - The Words That Change Everything
grow.content:
## Alhamdulillah - The Words That Change Everything

Have you ever said "Alhamdulillah" without really thinking about what it means? These aren't just words we say out of habit. They're magical words that can transform your entire life!

**Alhamdulillah** means "All praise is for Allah" or "Thank you, Allah, for everything."

### The Most Beautiful Words

The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) told us something incredible in Sahih Muslim: **"Alhamdulillah fills the scales (of good deeds)."**

Imagine that! Just by saying Alhamdulillah, you're filling up your book of good deeds. It's like collecting treasure for the afterlife, and all you have to do is say these beautiful words!

But there's more. Allah Himself says in the Quran: **"If you are grateful, I will surely increase you (in favor)."** (Quran 14:7)

Did you catch that? When you say Alhamdulillah and truly thank Allah, He promises to give you MORE blessings! It's the most amazing deal ever!

### The Secret the Prophets Knew

Do you know what Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) used to say when something good happened? **Alhamdulillah.**

What about when something bad happened? **Alhamdulillah.**

Wait, what? Even when something bad happens?

Yes! Because he understood something beautiful: Everything that happens is from Allah, and Allah only wants what's best for us. Sometimes what seems bad is actually good for us in ways we don't understand yet.

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said in Sahih Muslim: **"How wonderful is the affair of the believer, for all of his affairs are good. If something good happens to him, he is thankful and that is good for him. If something bad happens to him, he is patient and that is good for him."**

### A Heart Full of Thanks

Imam Ibn Qayyim, a great Islamic scholar, said something that will make you think: **"A person who thanks Allah is richer than a person who has everything but doesn't thank Allah."**

Think about it. You could have the biggest house, the coolest toys, all the video games in the world - but if you don't say Alhamdulillah, you'll never feel truly happy.

But someone who has just a little bit and says Alhamdulillah? Their heart is full of joy!

### Your Alhamdulillah Challenge

Starting today, try saying Alhamdulillah for these things:

**In the morning:**
- Alhamdulillah for waking up to a new day
- Alhamdulillah for your family
- Alhamdulillah for your health

**During the day:**
- Alhamdulillah when you eat something delicious
- Alhamdulillah when you understand something new at school
- Alhamdulillah when you laugh with your friends

**At night:**
- Alhamdulillah for making it through the day safely
- Alhamdulillah for your home and bed
- Alhamdulillah for everything you learned

### The Beautiful Truth

Here's something that might make you emotional: Every time you say Alhamdulillah, you're talking directly to Allah. You're telling the Creator of the Universe, "Thank You for thinking of me. Thank You for loving me. Thank You for giving me this."

And Allah hears every single word. Every. Single. Time.

So say it. Say it from your heart. Say it when you're happy. Say it even when you're sad. Because gratitude is the key that unlocks even more blessings.

**Alhamdulillah** - All praise is for Allah! 💚

---

### References

**Quran:**
- Surah Ibrahim (14:7) - "If you are grateful, I will surely increase you in favor"

**Authentic Hadith:**
- Sahih Muslim, Book 2 (The Book of Purification), Hadith 432 - "Alhamdulillah fills the scales (of good deeds)"
- Sahih Muslim, Book 55 (The Book of Zuhd and Softening of Hearts), Hadith 64 - "How wonderful is the affair of the believer, for all of his affairs are good. If something good happens to him, he is thankful and that is good for him. If something bad happens to him, he is patient and that is good for him."

**Scholars:**
- Imam Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyyah (1292-1350 CE) - On the richness of gratitude

grow.title: The Prophet Who Thanked Allah for Everything
grow.content:
## The Prophet Who Thanked Allah for Everything

### A Story That Will Touch Your Heart

Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) had a hard life. He lost his parents when he was very young. He lost his beloved wife Khadijah. He lost children. People hurt him, threw stones at him, and made fun of him.

But do you know what he did?

He thanked Allah. Again and again and again.

### The Night Prayer That Made His Feet Swell

Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), the Prophet's wife, tells us something amazing in Sahih Bukhari. She said the Prophet used to pray at night for SO LONG that his feet would swell up!

One night, she asked him: **"O Messenger of Allah, why do you do this when Allah has forgiven all your past and future sins?"**

His answer will make you cry. He said: **"Should I not be a grateful servant?"**

Let that sink in. The best human who ever lived, whose sins were already forgiven, still wanted to thank Allah MORE. He felt that everything Allah gave him deserved endless gratitude.

### What the Scholars Learned from Him

**Imam Ahmad's Gratitude in Pain**

Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal was a great scholar who was tortured for his beliefs. They beat him, whipped him, and put him in prison. It was so painful!

But you know what he said? **"Alhamdulillah."**

Why? Because he said: "Allah honored me by making me patient for His sake. How can I not thank Him?"

Even in pain, he found something to be grateful for!

**Ibn Taymiyyah in Prison**

Shaykh Ibn Taymiyyah was put in prison multiple times for teaching Islam. You'd think he'd be sad, right?

But he said something beautiful: **"What can my enemies do to me? My paradise is in my heart. If they put me in prison, it's my private time with Allah. If they exile me, it's tourism. If they kill me, it's martyrdom!"**

He was grateful in EVERY situation! That's the power of Alhamdulillah!

### The Gratitude That Heals

Here's something amazing: When you say Alhamdulillah, it actually makes you feel better!

Scientists have studied this (yes, really!). When people are grateful, they:
- Feel happier
- Sleep better
- Have less stress
- Make better friends
- Do better in school

But Muslims have known this for 1,400 years! The Prophet (peace be upon him) taught us that gratitude is the key to a happy life.

### Allah Loves Grateful People

The Quran tells us: **"And few of My servants are grateful."** (Quran 34:13)

Did you catch that? Allah is saying that not many people truly thank Him. This means when YOU say Alhamdulillah and really mean it, you're among the special few that Allah loves!

The Prophet (peace be upon him) also said in Sahih Bukhari: **"Allah is pleased with a servant who, when he eats something, thanks Allah for it, and when he drinks something, thanks Allah for it."**

Just by saying Alhamdulillah when you eat or drink, Allah is PLEASED with you. How easy is that?

### Be Like the Prophet

The Prophet (peace be upon him) would say Alhamdulillah:
- When he woke up
- When he ate
- When he drank
- When he wore new clothes
- When he heard good news
- When he overcame a difficulty
- Even when he sneezed!

If the best person to ever live said Alhamdulillah this much, what about us? We have so much to be grateful for!

### Your Mission This Week

Try to be like the Prophet (peace be upon him). Say Alhamdulillah at least 50 times today. Don't just count them - really feel them!

Thank Allah for:
- Your eyes that can see the beautiful sky
- Your ears that can hear birds singing
- Your family who loves you
- Your home that keeps you safe
- Your food that tastes delicious
- Your ability to learn new things

Every single one deserves an Alhamdulillah!

**Remember:** The Prophet (peace be upon him) with all his greatness still thanked Allah constantly. How much more should we? 💚

---

### References

**Quran:**
- Surah Saba (34:13) - "And few of My servants are grateful"

**Authentic Hadith:**
- Sahih Bukhari, Book 19 (Tahajjud), Hadith 1130 - Narration of Aisha (RA) about the Prophet's night prayers: "Should I not be a grateful servant?"
- Sahih Bukhari, Book 80 (Invocations), Hadith 7244 - "Allah is pleased with a servant who, when he eats something, thanks Allah for it, and when he drinks something, thanks Allah for it"
- Sahih Muslim, Book 49 (Book of Virtues), Hadith 2819 - Additional narration about the Prophet's lengthy night prayers

**Scholars:**
- Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal (780-855 CE) - His gratitude during the Mihna (Inquisition) persecution
- Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah (1263-1328 CE) - His gratitude while imprisoned in Damascus Citadel

grow.title: The Hidden Blessings You Never Notice
grow.content:
## The Hidden Blessings You Never Notice

### The Things We Take for Granted

Let me ask you something: When was the last time you said Alhamdulillah for your heartbeat?

Your heart beats about 100,000 times every single day. That's 100,000 times Allah is keeping you alive, and we don't even notice!

What about breathing? You breathe about 20,000 times a day without thinking about it. That's 20,000 gifts from Allah!

These are the hidden blessings - the ones we forget to thank Allah for because they're always there.

### The Scholar's Wake-Up Call

Imam Ibn al-Jawzi, a famous scholar, once said something powerful: **"If you woke up today with more health than sickness, you are more blessed than the million people who will not survive this week."**

He continued: **"If you have food in your fridge, clothes on your back, a roof over your head, and a place to sleep, you are richer than 75% of the world."**

Alhamdulillah! Do you see how blessed you are?

### The Test of Gratitude

Allah says in the Quran: **"And He gave you of all that you asked Him. And if you should count the favors of Allah, you could not enumerate them."** (Quran 14:34)

Try it right now. Try to count all your blessings. You can't! There are too many!

Your eyes, ears, nose, tongue, hands, feet, brain, family, friends, home, food, water, air, sun, moon, stars... the list goes on forever!

Each one deserves an Alhamdulillah, but we can't even count them all!

### What Happens When You Forget to Be Grateful?

The Prophet (peace be upon him) told us in Sahih Bukhari about people in the past who stopped being grateful. Allah took away their blessings because they didn't appreciate them.

But here's the beautiful part: It works the other way too! When you're grateful, Allah increases your blessings!

Remember the verse: **"If you are grateful, I will surely increase you."** (Quran 14:7)

It's a promise from Allah Himself!

### The Gratitude That Saved a Man

There's a beautiful story the scholars tell:

A man came to a wise teacher and said, "I'm so unhappy! I don't have much money. I don't have a big house. My life is so hard!"

The teacher asked, "Would you sell your eyes for a million dollars?"

"No!" said the man.

"Would you sell your hands for a million dollars?"

"Of course not!"

"What about your ability to walk? Your ability to hear? Your ability to speak?"

"No, no, no! I wouldn't sell any of them!"

The teacher smiled and said, **"Then you have millions of dollars worth of blessings already! Say Alhamdulillah!"**

The man started crying. He realized he was rich all along but never thanked Allah for it.

### The Special Blessings Nobody Thinks About

Shaykh Ibn Uthaymin used to remind people to say Alhamdulillah for:

**Safety** - You went to sleep and woke up safely. Many people didn't.

**Peace** - You're not in a war zone. You're not running from danger.

**Freedom** - You can pray, fast, and worship Allah without anyone stopping you.

**Parents** - Even if they're strict sometimes, they love you and take care of you!

**Education** - You can read this right now! Millions of kids around the world can't read.

**Clean Water** - You turn on a tap and water comes out. Some kids walk hours just to get dirty water.

Alhamdulillah! Alhamdulillah! Alhamdulillah!

### Your Gratitude Journal Challenge

For the next week, before you go to sleep, write down (or think about) 5 things you're grateful for that day. They can be big or small:

**Day 1 Example:**
1. Alhamdulillah for the delicious lunch I had
2. Alhamdulillah for making a friend laugh today
3. Alhamdulillah for my warm bed
4. Alhamdulillah for understanding my math homework
5. Alhamdulillah for my mom's hug

Do this every night. Watch how it changes the way you see your life!

### The Truth About Blessings

Here's something that might make you tear up:

Every blessing you have - every single one - is a love letter from Allah to you. He's saying, "I'm thinking about you. I care about you. I want you to be happy."

When you say Alhamdulillah, you're writing Him a thank-you note back.

And Allah loves when His servants thank Him.

So open your eyes. Look around. Count your blessings. And say it from your heart:

**Alhamdulillah. Alhamdulillah. Alhamdulillah.** 💚

---

*May Allah make us among those who are truly grateful, and may He increase us in His blessings. Ameen.* 🤲

---

### References

**Quran:**
- Surah Ibrahim (14:34) - "And He gave you of all that you asked Him. And if you should count the favors of Allah, you could not enumerate them"
- Surah Ibrahim (14:7) - "If you are grateful, I will surely increase you"
- Surah An-Nahl (16:18) - "And if you should count the favors of Allah, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful"

**Authentic Hadith:**
- Sahih Bukhari, Book 60 (Prophets), Hadith 3465 - Stories of past nations including those who were ungrateful
- Sahih Bukhari, Book 76 (Medicine), Hadith 5661 - "Take benefit of five before five: Your youth before your old age, your health before your sickness, your wealth before your poverty, your free time before you are preoccupied, and your life before your death"

**Scholars:**
- Imam Ibn al-Jawzi (1116-1201 CE) - From his book "Sayd al-Khatir" on the blessings of health and basic necessities
- Shaykh Muhammad ibn Salih al-Uthaymin (1925-2001 CE) - Reminders about hidden blessings from his various lectures and fatwas

grow.title: Alhamdulillah - Even When Things Are Hard
grow.content:
## Alhamdulillah - Even When Things Are Hard

### The Hardest Alhamdulillah

Saying Alhamdulillah when you get a new toy? Easy!

Saying Alhamdulillah when you ace a test? No problem!

But saying Alhamdulillah when you fail a test? When your friend hurts your feelings? When something you really wanted doesn't happen? That's when Alhamdulillah becomes powerful.

### The Prophet's Amazing Example

The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) faced the hardest situations anyone could face. But he taught us something incredible in Sahih Muslim:

**"How wonderful is the affair of the believer! All of his affairs are good for him. If something good happens, he is thankful, and that is good for him. If something bad happens, he is patient, and that is good for him."**

Did you catch that? EVERYTHING is good for the believer - even the hard things!

Why? Because when something difficult happens and you say Alhamdulillah and stay patient, you earn huge rewards from Allah!

### The Wisdom We Don't See

Allah says in the Quran: **"Perhaps you dislike something which is good for you, and perhaps you love something which is bad for you. Allah knows, and you do not know."** (Quran 2:216)

This is mind-blowing! Sometimes what we think is terrible is actually the best thing for us, and we just don't know it yet!

Let me tell you a story:

### The Broken Bike Story

A boy really wanted a new bike. He made du'a every day: "Ya Allah, please give me that bike!"

But it never happened. He felt sad. Why didn't Allah give it to him?

Years later, he found out that on the exact day he wanted to buy that bike, there was a recall - those bikes had a dangerous defect that caused serious accidents!

Allah didn't give him the bike because Allah was PROTECTING him!

Now imagine if he had said "Alhamdulillah" even when he didn't get what he wanted. He would have earned rewards AND been protected!

### What the Scholars Taught Us

**Umar ibn Al-Khattab's Beautiful Words**

Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), one of the greatest companions, said something amazing:

**"I have never been struck by a hardship except that I found four blessings in it:**
**1. It wasn't in my religion (my faith is still strong)**
**2. It could have been worse**
**3. It's a chance to earn rewards through patience**
**4. I hope Allah will reward me for it."**

Wow! He found FOUR reasons to say Alhamdulillah in every difficulty!

**Ibn Qayyim's Wisdom**

Imam Ibn Qayyim said: **"A calamity that makes you turn to Allah is better for you than a blessing that makes you forget Him."**

Think about it. Sometimes when life is too easy, we forget Allah. But when something hard happens and it makes us pray more, cry to Allah more, and remember Him more - that's actually a blessing in disguise!

### The Secret of True Believers

Here's a secret that will change your life:

True believers don't just thank Allah for the good things. They thank Allah IN the hard things, because they trust that Allah knows what's best.

It's not: "Why is this happening to me?"

It's: "What is Allah teaching me? What is He protecting me from? How can I grow from this?"

And always: "Alhamdulillah, Allah is with me."

### Your Tests Are Not Punishments

The Prophet (peace be upon him) said in Sahih Bukhari: **"No fatigue, disease, sorrow, sadness, hurt, or distress befalls a Muslim - even the prick of a thorn - except that Allah removes some of his sins because of it."**

Even a tiny thorn prick removes sins! 

So when something hard happens:
- Your sins are being erased
- Your rank in Paradise is increasing
- Allah is testing how much you trust Him
- You're becoming stronger

Alhamdulillah for all of it!

### How to Say Alhamdulillah in Hard Times

When something difficult happens, try this:

**Step 1:** Take a deep breath. It's okay to feel sad or disappointed. You're human!

**Step 2:** Remember Allah is testing you with this.

**Step 3:** Say: "Alhamdulillah. Allah knows what's best for me."

**Step 4:** Make du'a: "Ya Allah, I don't understand why this happened, but I trust You. Please make it easy for me and help me learn from it."

**Step 5:** Look for the hidden blessing. It's always there, even if you can't see it yet.

### The Most Beautiful Promise

Allah promises in the Quran: **"Indeed, with hardship comes ease. Indeed, with hardship comes ease."** (Quran 94:5-6)

He said it TWICE! That's how important it is!

No matter how hard things are right now, ease is coming. Allah promised. And Allah never breaks His promises.

### Your Life-Changing Challenge

This week, when something doesn't go your way - maybe you don't get picked for the team, or you get a bad grade, or someone is mean to you - try this:

Instead of complaining, say: **"Alhamdulillah. I trust Allah's plan."**

Watch how it changes your feelings. Watch how it gives you peace. Watch how it makes you stronger.

### The Final Truth

You know what the difference is between a happy person and a sad person?

It's not how many blessings they have.

It's whether they say Alhamdulillah or not.

Two people can have the same life. One complains about what they don't have. The other thanks Allah for what they do have.

Guess which one is happier?

The one who says Alhamdulillah!
